section_summary: This section documents efforts in 1946 to convince Japanese residents of São Paulo state that Japan had surrendered. Consular reports, telegrams, newspaper shipments, film-showing reports, and a lengthy FBI account describe the campaign and continuing violence attributed to Shindo Renmei. The final pages contain a list of 187 proposed letters between residents of Brazil and addressees in Japan.

subfiles.title: First visit of sound truck into interior with Japanese films
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on Japanese-language film showings in São Paulo state's interior.
subfiles.summary: Says Japanese newspapers drew more interest than the available films and urges recognizable occupation footage and direct correspondence with Japan.

subfiles.title: Visit of sound truck with Japanese films to interior towns
subfiles.to: American Consulate General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Reports audiences, police cooperation, and newspaper distribution during film showings.
subfiles.summary: Showings took place in Pompéia, Tupã, Bastos, and Lucélia; Marília police refused permission. Newspapers often interested Japanese attendees more than the films, and police deputies favored renewed correspondence with relatives in Japan. Page 214 repeats part of the text on page 216.

subfiles.title: Reports on Japanese nationalist leaders
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports that nationalist leaders may continue their campaign despite knowing Japan lost.
subfiles.summary: Leaders reportedly hoped friction with Russia might improve Japan's position.

subfiles.title: Messages and broadcasts from Japan for Brazil
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports progress and delays in preparing messages, films, and broadcasts for Japanese in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Postal messages were being assembled, but shortages delayed Japanese-produced radio recordings and films. The adviser asked whether work should continue after reports that terrorist leaders had acknowledged defeat.

subfiles.title: Receipt and distribution of Japanese newspapers
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges newspaper shipments and requests that they continue.
subfiles.summary: The consulate distributed the papers with police and community assistance. It reported favorable responses, especially to small-town Japanese papers, and enclosed a press clipping.

subfiles.title: Jornais japoneses em grande quantidade para os nipônicos do interior
subfiles.about: Describes distribution of Japanese newspapers to residents of São Paulo state's interior.
subfiles.summary: The clipping reports a new consular shipment of roughly 2,000 papers and cooperation with São Paulo public security officials. It connects the distribution to efforts to counter Shindo Renmei violence and convince Japanese residents of Japan's surrender.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-191 on Japanese societies in Brazil
subfiles.to: American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Repeats Tokyo's inquiry and asks whether Japanese societies have acknowledged defeat.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests confirmation of a reported manifesto, the consulate's views on continuing messages and broadcasts, and advice on further newspaper and film shipments.

subfiles.title: Postal cards for Japanese residents of Brazil
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards postal cards prepared by correspondents in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses 29 stamped, canceled, and censored cards for rapid transmission to São Paulo.

subfiles.title: Forwarding 29 postal cards to São Paulo
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Sends 29 postal cards received from Japan for discretionary delivery.
subfiles.summary: The Department hopes their receipt will help the Japanese community accept the surrender.

subfiles.title: Repetition of São Paulo airgram A-211 to Tokyo
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Repeats São Paulo's assessment of its campaign against surrender denial.
subfiles.summary: The quoted airgram says newspapers have worked best, more occupation footage is needed, and sustained correspondence and broadcasts may help convince remaining skeptics.

subfiles.title: Return of letters intended for Japan
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Returns 69 private letters previously submitted for diplomatic forwarding.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites the reopening of limited private mail service to Japan.

subfiles.title: São Paulo airgram A-211 on the Japanese situation
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Assesses the effect of sound-truck films and Japanese newspaper distribution.
subfiles.summary: The consulate reports quieter conditions but continuing disbelief among many Japanese residents. It asks for more newspapers and occupation footage, and expects direct letters and sustained radio broadcasts to help.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal of report on Japanese societies in Brazil
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon; Chief of Naval Intelligence; Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2
subfiles.about: Transmits an intelligence report concerning Japanese societies in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends the attached report to State, Navy, and War Department recipients.

subfiles.title: Japanese societies in Brazil
subfiles.about: Investigates Shindo Renmei, associated groups, murders, police action, and surrender-denial propaganda in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: The report identifies Japanese nationalist societies, describes killings and attempted killings of people who acknowledged Japan's defeat, and lists 80 alleged leaders marked for expulsion. It recounts Brazilian police investigations, the questioned role of Kishimoto, the society's program, and a contentious meeting at the governor's palace. It also evaluates newspaper distribution and explains why some Japanese residents misread surrender photographs as proof of victory.

subfiles.title: Correspondence for Japan
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests diplomatic forwarding of letters because Brazilian post offices still refuse mail for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross says families in Brazil await replies and that correspondence could ease continuing tension. He encloses letters, postage, and a list of senders and addressees; page 270 is a duplicate text copy.

subfiles.title: List of addressees and addressers for letters to Japan
subfiles.to: Department of State
subfiles.about: Lists proposed Japanese addressees and Brazilian senders for 187 letters.
subfiles.summary: The numbered list gives names and addresses across 38 Japanese prefectures and Brazilian locations, principally São Paulo state. It accompanied the consulate's request to forward private letters while ordinary mail from Brazil to Japan remained closed.
